A broader packed_refs substring probe also matched one unrelated packed lookup fixture and failed because gix-ref/tests/fixtures/packed-refs/triggers-out-of-bounds was not materialized in the sparse cache. Full workspace cargo test was not executed because it would hydrate and build the large feature-heavy workspace beyond the current VM cap.

Next slice should add more focused upstream gix-merge fixtures, more rename heuristics, credential prompt fallback semantics, or controlled crate-level upstream runner evidence. The proxy credential lifecycle slice maps helper-returned credentials to store/erase callbacks after successful or failed smart HTTP requests, and the later default requester SOCKS slice covers native SOCKS handshakes. The default PHP requester now implements native SOCKS4/SOCKS4a/SOCKS5/SOCKS5h CONNECT handshakes for smart HTTP receive-pack over HTTP and HTTPS, including TLS peer verification through a configured CA file for HTTPS-over-SOCKS discovery. The latest commit-token iterator slice maps gix-object CommitRefIter token order, SHA-256 token IDs, multi-line extra-header tokens, message tokens, and partial error returns after prior successful tokens. The previous commit-signature slice maps gix-object/gix-actor actor parsing boundaries, including SHA-256 commit IDs, trimmed author/committer accessors, lenient malformed email delimiter handling, complete timestamp consumption, encoding, and multiline gpgsig headers, and now maps commit message summary/title/body parsing, trailer block heuristics, attribution filters, pgp_signature access, and signed-data extraction that removes the signature header bytes. The latest BodyRef commit-message slice maps gix-object MessageRef/BodyRef title-body splitting with LF/CRLF and inconsistent separators, retained title-only trailing newlines, empty bodies, sole-body trailers, folded trailers, exact/below-threshold recognized-prefix footer rules, generic trailer-looking prose rejection, and standalone body trailer parsing for WordPress review notes. The latest annotated-tag slice maps gix-object TagRef parsing for SHA-1/SHA-256 targets, target kind validation, optional taggers, empty/missing separator messages, line-boundary PGP signature detection, and commit mergetag parsing into native tag objects. The latest annotated-tag write slice maps Gitoxide WriteTo semantics for tag body roundtrips, all-newline messages, PGP signature emission, size accounting, and tag name validation, while exposing an ordered token stream for WordPress release provenance. The latest annotated-tag ref-iterator slice preserves raw uppercase object-header bytes separately from normalized object IDs, exposes partial token results before decode errors, and updates the WordPress signed release-tag fixture so provenance hashes roundtrip exact tag bytes. Full raw byte-range token borrowing and broader owned-vs-borrowed tag writer parity remain future work. The latest commit trailer byte-class slice treats vertical tab as upstream whitespace for trailer blank separators, folded trailer continuations, and leading/trailing trailer value trim, while preserving Gitoxide summary-fold behavior that keeps a vertical tab immediately before an internal newline. The latest commit write slice maps gix-object CommitRef::write_to output, size(), and commit object kind by emitting canonical commit storage bytes, object-wrapping them, and exposing WordPress import/deploy commit storage/object hashes. The latest tag-name sanitization slice maps gix-validate byte-level sanitize behavior into GitTag::sanitizeName and adds WordPress draft release-tag normalization before tag construction. The bounded upstream runner evidence is crate-level only: gix-object --lib passed 10 tests, but full workspace and gix-object integration-test parity remain open. The latest reference-name slice maps gix-ref FullNameRef category/short-name helpers, Category::to_full_name construction, namespace expansion/prefix/strip helpers, and a WordPress deployment reference classification fixture for local, remote-tracking, tag, pseudo, main-worktree, linked-worktree, worktree-private, and namespaced refs. The latest reference validation slice maps gix_validate::reference::name complete-name semantics: slash-containing names like `heads/main`/`hello/world` are valid, standalone names must be uppercase pseudo refs, and malformed push/ad advertisement guard tests now reject truly invalid standalone lowercase refs. The latest commit parser slice tightens Commit::parse() to follow gix-object decode::commit header order instead of accepting standard commit headers anywhere in the header block; late parent/encoding names are now exposed as extra headers, matching the upstream parser boundary. The namespaced reference-store iteration slice maps gix-ref store namespace transparency: store iteration and loose iteration strip the namespace, prefix iteration works store-relative, packed refs are filtered through the store namespace, symbolic targets inside the namespace are stripped, and redundant namespaced lookups miss in a namespace-aware store. The latest reference transaction slices map PreviousValue-style update/delete guards, namespace-transparent loose reference writes/deletes, packed-ref delete/update rewrites, default loose shadow updates for packed refs, explicit packed update modes that leave or prune loose source refs, all-packed delete removal of packed-refs, object-update reflog append lines, reflog deletion, peeled-tag object lookup for packed updates, and deref update/delete splitting where symbolic parents become log-only edits, update leaves receive object writes, and delete reflog-only leaves remove parent plus leaf reflogs while preserving both refs. Lock rollback and full filesystem-lock semantics remain unported. The latest TagRef-to-owned slice maps the Gitoxide boundary where borrowed TagRef write_to preserves raw parsed target bytes, TagRef::into_owned parses the target into an ObjectId, and owned Tag write_to emits normalized object IDs after conversion. The WordPress annotated-tag fixture now proves parsed uppercase release-tag targets roundtrip exactly, generated draft release tags use canonical lowercase object IDs, and parsed imported tags can be converted to owned canonical tag bytes through GitTag::toOwned(). The latest smart HTTP followRedirects slice maps Gitoxide HTTP FollowRedirects::Initial/All/None semantics into PHP options: default/initial follows only discovery redirects, false/none rejects redirects, and true/all permits safe same-host receive-pack POST redirects while preserving the generated request body. The latest gix-credentials context slice maps credential helper context encoding/decoding, blank-line termination, quit boolean parsing, URL destructuring, prompt/display URL helpers, and secret redaction/clearing for deployment logs. The latest gix-credentials cascade slice maps helper ordering, partial credential merge and overwrite, failed-helper continuation, helper URL destructuring, expired credential clearing, quit handling, query-user-only bogus password boundaries, and store/erase payload fan-out without invoking git credential. The latest gix-credentials helper-program slice maps builtin/external action argument names, helper-name and absolute-path declarations, `!script` declarations, shell-vs-argv boundaries, and shell `$@` forwarding without invoking helper processes.

The latest commit-token iterator slice maps gix-object CommitRefIter order for tree, parent, author, committer, encoding, extraHeader, and message tokens, including SHA-256 token IDs, multi-line extra-header values, and partial error results after prior successful tokens. The latest slice maps core.bigFileThreshold-style oversized text blobs to binary-style recursive conflict handling. The latest slice maps exact file rename/modify clean resolution for the upstream simple side-1-3-without-conflict fixture in both merge directions. The latest slice maps the simple fast-forward/no-change/unrelated clean merges, simple single-content-conflict fixture and diff3 variant, keeping greeting unresolved while cleanly merging the numbers file and preserving the one-sided whatever edit. The latest slice maps the simple side-1-2-various-conflicts fixture and diff3 variant, combining a clean line merge with content-conflict marker output and file/directory relocated staging. The latest slice maps simple tweak1-side2 and its diff3 variant, and upgrades file rename/modify handling so edited renamed files merge at the target path with regular content-conflict stages. The latest slice maps the both-modify-file-with-binary-attr fixture, preserving pseudo-binary text conflict output with marker blobs and staged ancestor/ours/theirs entries. The latest slice maps the super-1 cyclic rename/rename target collision fixture, materializing colliding rename targets with marker blobs and staged ancestor/ours/theirs entries. The latest slice maps the super-2 directory/file collision fixture by relocating the file side to `~B`, preserving the directory side, and staging the relocated file for review. The latest slice maps the simple fast-forward, no-change, side-1-unrelated, and side-1-unrelated-diff3 fixture shapes to prove clean tree output and empty conflict/index/worktree views. The latest slice maps gix-transport curl proxy type/auth-method handling by accepting http, https, socks, socks4, socks4a, socks5, and socks5h proxy declarations, normalizing anyauth/basic/digest/negotiate/ntlm auth method names, exposing SOCKS proxy options to injected requesters, and explicitly rejecting SOCKS use in the default PHP stream requester until a native handshake layer exists. The latest slice maps gix-transport curl proxy credential lifecycle semantics: credentials returned by proxyCredentialHelper are stored after a successful smart HTTP request and erased after failed authentication/request failure while keeping Proxy-Authorization out of origin headers. The latest slice replaces the prior default-stream SOCKS blocker with native SOCKS4/SOCKS4a/SOCKS5/SOCKS5h CONNECT handshakes, including SOCKS5 username/password authentication and SOCKS4a remote DNS, while keeping proxy credentials out of tunneled origin HTTP headers. The latest slice maps gix-transport TLS options for smart HTTP by accepting sslCaInfo and sslVerify, applying CA/peer verification to PHP stream contexts, and verifying HTTPS receive-pack discovery through a SOCKS5h tunnel after CONNECT without leaking proxy headers to the origin request. The previous commit-signature slice adds SHA-256-aware commit object ID validation, author/committer signature accessors, gix-actor-style delimiter parsing, timestamp seconds/offset helpers, encoding and multiline extra-header exposure, and a WordPress import/deploy commit provenance fixture. The latest commit-message slice maps gix-object MessageRef summary folding, title/body splitting with LF and CRLF separators, BodyRef trailer-block detection heuristics, folded trailer values, Signed-off-by/Co-authored-by/Reviewed-by attribution filters, pgp_signature access, and signed-data extraction that removes gpgsig header bytes while preserving the rest of the commit body. The latest annotated-tag slice maps gix-object TagRef parsing for annotated tags, including SHA-256 targets, optional taggers, empty messages, PGP signature line-boundary splitting, malformed tag, and commit mergetag headers as native tag objects. The latest annotated-tag write slice adds Gitoxide-style tag storage byte emission, exact size accounting, native tag object construction, ordered token exposure, writer-side tag-name validation, upstream-shaped signed/empty tag roundtrips, and a WordPress signed release-tag provenance fixture. The latest annotated-tag ref-iterator slice maps Gitoxide TagRef raw target preservation and TagRefIter partial-error behavior: parsed tags keep normalized target IDs for identity while retaining raw object header bytes for storage-byte roundtrips, token iteration emits no-tagger placeholders, and partial tags return earlier successful tokens plus a decode error marker. The latest commit-message slice adds vertical-tab trailer byte-class parity against gix-object body.rs and bstr trimming semantics. The latest actor timestamp/accessor slice maps gix-actor SignatureRef and gix-date raw header behavior: CommitSignature::time() exposes parsed seconds plus offset, accepts offset seconds, defaults malformed offsets to UTC, preserves raw malformed offset bytes for storage roundtrips, keeps missing timestamps invalid for full time parsing, and rejects invalid signature write tokens. The latest reference namespace slice maps gix-ref Namespace::into_namespaced_prefix by appending a relative iteration prefix to expanded namespace bytes while preserving trailing slashes for WordPress multisite review-branch scans. The latest reference-store slice maps gix-ref packed transaction boundaries: packed deletes rewrite or remove packed-refs, loose deletes also remove stale packed overlays, default packed updates write loose shadows, explicit packed update modes rewrite sorted packed-refs, can prune loose source refs, peel tag objects through ObjectDatabase, and object updates/deletes append or remove Git-shaped reflog files. The latest deref transaction slice maps gix-ref update preprocessing where `HEAD` remains symbolic, its edit is reported as reflog-only, the leaf branch receives the object update, and both reflogs use the leaf object transition. The latest gix-credentials slice adds native credential-helper context parsing and serialization, URL destructuring, prompt/display URL helpers, quit parsing, and secret redaction/clearing. The latest credential-cascade slice maps helper ordering, partial credential merge/overwrite, expired secret clearing, quit handling, query-user-only, and store/erase fan-out.

wordpressScenario: Git-backed WordPress content workflows, package installs, Playground snapshots, and server-side repo primitives; current examples parse a WordPress deploy tree, write/read HEAD plus deployment branch refs, inspect packed branch/tag refs, parse protocol v2 ls-refs discovery responses, build a shallow blobless ref-in-want fetch request, parse protocol v2 fetch response sections and sideband pack/progress/error bytes, orchestrate a protocol v1 send-pack flow from advertised refs through generated branch/tag pack request and status response, build thin REF_DELTA send-pack payloads against remote WordPress base objects, run receive-pack handshake/request/response cycles over native stream, git-daemon, smart HTTP auth/session/redirect/proxy/SOCKS declaration, and SSH command adapters, resolve loose+packed refs, locate compacted object offsets through pack indexes and multi-pack-indexes, use MIDX-backed object database pack selection/de-duplication, read delta-resolved packed commit/blob objects, track blobless partial-clone promisor state for omitted media objects, lazily hydrate promised media objects into loose storage, apply sparse checkout materialization to a plugin-focused WordPress tree, recursively merge nested WordPress metadata/theme blobs with Git index v2 conflict-stage writes, checkout-clean merged worktree marker-file output, stale file removal, .git metadata preservation, directory-file tree-stage index expansion, exact same-object rename/delete and rename/rename conflicts, bounded similar-blob rename/delete and rename/modify conflicts for renamed plugin entry files, same-target rename content merges at the renamed plugin path, bounded directory rename/modify merges for renamed plugin directories, directory rename heuristics that match renamed plugin entry files and choose strict-best forked plugin directory candidates, and pack+loose+alternate object database traversal with replacement refs without shelling out to git. Credential scenarios now cover helper context exchange, helper cascade store/erase, and helper-program command preflight for credential-cache, credential-oauth, absolute tenant helpers, and builtin git credential actions without invoking git credential. The latest WordPress credential-program example maps Gitoxide helper definitions into command arguments before any helper process is invoked.
